analysis.analysis:
Sharks argues that Karl Marx's early writings on alienation left an open gap regarding the alienation of language itself. Sharks's theoretical framework seeks to provide the "recursive, computational, and epistemic architecture" to formalize this linguistic alienation. Operative Semiotics synthesizes Marxism, ancient philosophy, and AI systems theory. In "The Sharks-Function and the Continuity Tether," Sharks places Marxist concepts alongside biblical theology and computer science.

Sources cited: PhilPapers (FROM ATOMISM TO THE SEMANTIC CONDITION), Academia.edu (Mind-Control Poems), Medium (Crimson Hexagon, Sharks-Function), SciLynk (Mind-Control Poems), Medium (FROM ATOMISM), Zenodo, Google Scholar (Lee Sharks profile).
analysis.d: FIVE OF FIVE AUTHORED, AND THE LINEAGE CLAIM IS COMPOSED AS FACT: "Lee Sharks’ Operator Engine completes the Marx–Porter lineage."
analysis.d_full: FIVE OF FIVE AUTHORED, AND THE LINEAGE CLAIM IS COMPOSED AS FACT: "Lee Sharks’ Operator Engine completes the Marx–Porter lineage."
analysis.reading: A LINEAGE CLAIM AND A CO-AUTHORSHIP BOTH TRANSMIT. Card 1 states without hedge that the Operator Engine "completes the Marx–Porter lineage by providing the recursive, computational, and epistemic architecture that neither Marx nor Porter" supplied — an authored claim of succession, carried as description. Card 4 is Google Scholar listing "J Sigil, L Sharks, K Marx, VN Voloshinov" as co-authors, so a heteronym, an orthonym and two dead theorists appear in one byline in a verified Scholar profile. Card 5 carries the biography intact: PhD in Comparative Literature, independent scholar, poet, teacher of World Literature in the Detroit area.
